[quote=the_commonwealth_provisional_states;61756858]"Hmmm...I will take....a Big Mac and a large fry, I suppose. On second thought, I will take a Nuka Cherry with that as well," Julian says, sitting down

"Man, you know how long it's been since I've eaten fast food...like actual fast food?" He remarks

"Like sure, I can request it. But it has to be made in the White Mansion; the Secret Service won't let me even eat food that isn't cooked there sometimes. Quite annoying. Hey...now that I think about it" He looks at King Henri

"Why'd you invite me to this, seems...odd for a diplomatic meeting."[/quote]

Henri nodded, "You were invited to this because it is a representation, a manifestation of a new era, in my eyes. You see, History is the study of the past; it is the series of events that led to the present state of our world. We have lived within it since our creation, and have moved through its parameters (this being time and space) for as long as the first man was made. 

Now, to the human eye, history unfolds in a linear model, A leads to B, and so on and so on, thereby making history a domino effect from which the creator placed down his hand and knocked over the first domino. However, if history were truly a linear progression of events leading to an inevitable end, why do we humans wonder about counterfactuals, and why do we have choices?

Some might say the choices we make are inevitable, fate, to use the humanistic term; however, I object to this usage, because if it were simply fate, then why make choices at all, because at the end of the day, fate would just re-order the timeline. 

However, we do make choices, and we do have counterfactuals, and events that shouldve happened dont happen, and events which, to the logical mind, shouldnt happen do happen. Thus, the domino theory falls to the wayside and is rendered null by our very own free will. 

Now, some say history repeats itself, and suggest that history is just a series of circles looping in on themselves, going from point A to point B and then C and then A1 and so on, rendering merely variations of events in different times across the span of our existences. This is not something I necessarily disagree with; however, I do tend that while yes, history does repeat itself, it doesnt repeat itself because it is inevitable in being bound to do so (for this is merely a re-statement of the domino theory), but because the particular set of events which led to event A happening, happened in such a way to allow A1 to happen and resemble event A. However, this doesnt explain that even though A1 did happen, it doesnt resemble event A. 

It is in this that we must examine historical events not as isolated dots on a linear plot, but as multiple dots on a multi-planar field, interconnected in various means and manners.

Now you may ask, how does this relate to your question? Well, history has aligned itself through the various nodalities in such a manner that we are now sitting at this table, ushering in this new era."

[i][b]Official Statement of the United States of Oceanica
On National Transition, Foreign Policy, and Economic Direction[/b]

There is an official shift in the positions foreign relations, governance, and international policy of the United States of Oceanica. The United States of Oceanica will continue to be a Liberal Democratic Federal Commonwealth that will be governed through its constitution with a politically involved citizenry inculcated with a conservative civic culture along with well planned multiculturalism. Democracy will continue to thrive in the country with the federal states functioning efficiently through a system that allows private businesses and development plans with foresight to succeed. The United States of Oceanica will continue to have an economic system that will consist of a mixed capitalism in which innovations will flourish along with selective governmental control in sectors like technology, energy, finance, and infrastructure.

In this regard, the USO will be retiring from its full membership within the EDU and assume the status of an associate member. Such a move has been motivated by the need for adopting an approach to avoid the ongoing increase in geopolitical tensions and associated conflicts that have become more bloc-like in nature. Although the country will continue to pursue its historical and diplomatic relations with EDU members, it will not be involved in any foreign wars or military actions. Rather, it will be assuming a neutral stance while ensuring its sovereignty and maintaining stability in its national territory.

Such a neutral stance does not mean the isolation of the country from other nations; rather, it means that the USO will be positioning itself as an open and safe international center of financial, business, and political transactions. At the same time, it will be working hard at improving economic partnerships with different countries all over the world, both within and outside the EDU group of nations.
From an economic standpoint, the USO will become an economic powerhouse by virtue of developing a highly technological and innovative nature. It will prioritize semiconductor manufacturing, nuclear science, cyber-security systems, computational and electronic engineering. Other economic priorities will include manufacturing innovations, computing and engineering, high-quality electronic equipment, etc. All the above-mentioned sectors play a pivotal role in the formation of the economic image of Oceanica and provide its significance in terms of being one of the worlds most relevant suppliers of goods and technologies.

In addition to the priority economic sectors mentioned above, USO will also retain economic diversification in logistics, construction, finance and energy sectors. Trade systems will undergo necessary modernizations that will help USO operate as an international commercial crossroad in cases of global instability. This approach will guarantee national security in terms of economic sustainability of the country.

In spite of being a neutral state and refraining from entering any foreign conflict, USO will still possess the necessary military potential that can be used to defend the countrys territory, citizens, and economic stability against any foreign threats.

It will also place Oceanica into a different functional relationship with the international community. As an independent yet advanced nation state, Oceanica will be the foundation for diplomatic action, the safe-haven for international business dealings, and the nexus for innovation and technology. Those nations that wish to pursue collaboration, business, and negotiation can do so on the basis that this is done in harmony with the tenets of law and peace.

This does not signify an end but rather the continuation of activities under a new paradigm. The United States of Oceanica will continue to exist as a political and diplomatic force to be reckoned with on the international scene. It will do so through consistency in policy, behavior, and moderation. All further activity by the United States of Oceanica will adhere to this model until a national change in direction is officially stated.
[/i]
